claims.statement: `services/` contains exactly two independent Go modules — `indicator-service` and `mcp-gateway` — each with its own `go.mod` and dependency tree (`indicator-service` requires only `github.com/cinar/indicator/v2`; `mcp-gateway` requires `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` plus indirect modules).

There is deliberately no shared Go module across the services: a shared internal module was evaluated and rejected because the services have distinct lifecycles and minimal code overlap, and sharing code would create version lockstep and cross-service coupling; conventions are shared through `services/README.md` instead.

Each service follows the `cmd/<service>/` + `internal/` layout: `cmd/<service>/main.go` holds entrypoint wiring only (config load, logger, router/server, lifecycle), and all other packages live under `internal/`, which Go's package visibility rules make unimportable from other modules.

Service domain packages stay free of HTTP concerns: `services/indicator-service/internal/indicators` (calculator, spec/parameter resolution, `ScalePeriod`) imports no `net/http`, keeping the indicator math independent of the transport that exposes it, while HTTP concerns stay in `internal/httpapi`.

Both services parse configuration through an injected lookup function — `config.Load(getenv func(string) string) (Config, error)`, invoked in `main` as `config.Load(os.Getenv)` — so parsing and validation rules are unit-testable without mutating the process environment.

Configuration loading is fail-fast and names the offending variable in its error: a missing required value or an invalid format (`LOG_LEVEL`, `MAX_CONCURRENCY`, `SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, `BACKEND_BASE_URL`) aborts startup, and `mcp-gateway`'s configuration errors never echo the service-token value.

Configuration surfaces differ per service: `indicator-service` reads only optional `PORT` (default `8080`), `ENVIRONMENT` (default `dev`) and `LOG_LEVEL`; `mcp-gateway` additionally requires `BACKEND_BASE_URL` (validated as an http/https origin with a host) and `MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN`, and accepts optional `DATA_PLANE_PATH`/`MARKET_DATA_PATH` (default `/api/v1/market/data`, `DATA_PLANE_PATH` winning), `MAX_CONCURRENCY` (default `10`) and `SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT` (default `30m`).

The startup failure channel diverges: `indicator-service` writes its configuration error to `os.Stderr` and calls `os.Exit(1)` because no logger exists yet, while `mcp-gateway` reports it with `slog.Error` against the default logger before `logging.Init` installs the configured one.

Both services select log handlers identically: `ENVIRONMENT=prod` uses `slog.NewJSONHandler` with default level `INFO`, dev or unset uses `slog.NewTextHandler` with default level `DEBUG`, and a valid `LOG_LEVEL` (`DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN`/`WARNING`, `ERROR`) overrides the default while an invalid value fails configuration loading.

`mcp-gateway`'s `logging.Init(cfg)` sets the constructed logger as the `slog` default, and `main` derives a service-scoped logger carrying `service`, `port`, `backend_url`, `data_plane_path`, `environment` and `max_concurrency` so every subsequent record inherits them.

Log level and environment gate different debug paths: `indicator-service`'s `/compute` body dump and `mcp-gateway`'s outbound request/response traces plus tool invocation/completion records are gated by log level alone and reappear under `LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` in prod, whereas `mcp-gateway`'s inbound headers/query/body dump is gated on `ENVIRONMENT=dev` via `config.IsDev` and never appears in prod.

Both services wrap their router in access-logging middleware that captures the final status code through a wrapping `http.ResponseWriter` exposing `Unwrap` and emits one completion record per request with `method`, `path`, `status` and `duration`; `indicator-service` applies it inside `httpapi.NewRouter`, while `mcp-gateway` applies it in `main` around the router returned by `server.NewRouter`.

`indicator-service` derives the access-log severity from the response status (`>= 500` → `ERROR`, `>= 400` → `WARN`, otherwise `INFO`) and, when `DEBUG` is enabled, additionally reads and re-buffers the request body (up to 10MB) to log it for `/compute`.

`mcp-gateway` currently logs every request completion at `INFO` with `remote_addr` and `status` as fields rather than deriving severity from the status, and in dev it emits a `DEBUG` inbound record with `headers`, `query` and the body (truncated at 64KB) after redacting `Authorization`, `X-Service-Token`, `Cookie` and `Set-Cookie` to `[REDACTED]`.

`mcp-gateway`'s logging response writer tracks bytes written and implements `http.Flusher` pass-through, so streamable HTTP SSE responses flush immediately instead of being buffered by the middleware.

`indicator-service` implements the `X-Request-ID` contract: it propagates an incoming header or generates an RFC 4122 version 4 UUID from `crypto/rand` (falling back to a `req-<unix-nano>` string only if the entropy read fails), echoes the value on the response, and stores both the ID and a logger pre-populated with `request_id` in the request context for handlers to read via `RequestIDFromContext`/`LoggerFromContext`.
`mcp-gateway` has not implemented `X-Request-ID` propagation or a `request_id` log field; `services/README.md` records that adoption as pending work tied to its OpenTelemetry tracing follow-up.

Both services shut down gracefully on `SIGHUP`, `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM` or `SIGQUIT`: a shutdown goroutine creates a context with a hard-coded 10-second deadline, calls `http.Server.Shutdown`, and cancels `serverCtx` so `main` unblocks; a watcher goroutine logs when the deadline expires before connections drain (`WARN` in `indicator-service`, `ERROR` in `mcp-gateway`), and a `Shutdown` error is logged separately as `server shutdown error`.

Startup errors are fatal but `http.ErrServerClosed` is not: any other `ListenAndServe` error is logged and exits `1`, while a clean shutdown returns from `main` (exit `0`) after logging that the service stopped.

`http.Server` timeouts are per-service: `indicator-service` sets 15s read, 15s write and 60s idle, while `mcp-gateway` sets 15s read, `WriteTimeout: 0` (unlimited) deliberately so MCP streamable HTTP SSE responses are not truncated mid-stream, and 60s idle.

Neither listener authenticates or rate-limits: `indicator-service` is documented as internal-only and never publicly exposed, and `mcp-gateway`'s `/mcp` is unauthenticated by design because the shared-secret trust boundary is the backend data plane (`X-Service-Token` on outbound calls), not the MCP listener.

`mcp-gateway` wraps `/mcp` in `http.NewCrossOriginProtection()`, so browser cross-origin requests carrying `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` or a mismatched `Origin` receive `403 Forbidden`, while non-browser MCP agents without those headers connect normally.

Dev Compose publishes each Go service only on the host loopback (`127.0.0.1:${INDICATOR_SERVICE_PORT:-8004}` and `127.0.0.1:${MCP_GATEWAY_PORT:-8005}` mapped to container `8080`), and prod Compose publishes no host port for either service.

Service tokens and other secrets never reach logs or error strings in `mcp-gateway`: configuration errors name the variable but not the value, inbound request-log header dumps replace `Authorization`, `X-Service-Token`, `Cookie` and `Set-Cookie` with `[REDACTED]`, outbound transport logging omits the token, and tests assert the token header is absent from log output.

Diagnostic backend detail stays on the Go side in `mcp-gateway`: truncated status/body detail is retained on the error for logging only and is excluded from `Error()` and from user-facing MCP tool results, while a parsed backend `422` validation message is forwarded so the caller can retry with corrected parameters.

Provider-agnostic vocabulary is an enforced rule for the whole `mcp-gateway` module: tool names, titles, descriptions, input schemas, results, errors and log lines must not mention an upstream provider brand, and dedicated compliance tests assert this over server metadata, the tool registry, tool results, validation errors and log output.

Both Dockerfiles build the same way: a `golang:1.27-alpine` builder downloads modules first for layer caching and runs `CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o <service> ./cmd/<service>`, and an `alpine:3.21` runtime installs `ca-certificates tzdata wget`, runs as the unprivileged `appuser`, exposes port `8080` and healthchecks `wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/health` every 30s with a 5s timeout, 3 retries and a 5s start period.

`indicator-service` is a stateless calculator that owns no data: it serves `GET /health` and `POST /compute`, computes requested indicator series from candles supplied in the request body, keys the response map by each spec's `ResultKey()` (its `id` when set, otherwise its `type`), and returns an empty array rather than an error when there are too few candles.

`mcp-gateway` is a thin transport layer: it holds no provider credentials, reaches providers only through the backend data plane at `BACKEND_BASE_URL + DATA_PLANE_PATH` with the `X-Service-Token` header, and centralizes outbound calls in `backend.Transport` with a 15s HTTP timeout, a semaphore sized by `MAX_CONCURRENCY`, an 8MiB response cap, and `RouteGroup`-scoped path prefixes and tokens.

`mcp-gateway`'s extension points are a new `transport.NewRouteGroup` for an additional data plane, a per-domain client under `internal/backend`, and a per-family `register<Family>Tools` function called from `tools.Register`; `addTool` with a `toolSpec` annotates every tool with `ReadOnlyHint: true`, `IdempotentHint: true` and a title.

Go checks run on the host toolchain or via `just` rather than inside Docker: `just lint-go` runs a `gofmt -l` check over both service directories and then `staticcheck@v0.8.1` and `govulncheck@v1.8.0` in each module; `just test-indicator-service` and `just test-mcp-gateway` run `go test ./...` per module; `just test-all` runs backend, frontend, both Go suites and the Node script tests in parallel; `just check` adds Gate 0 for the auto-detected ecosystems.

CI runs two independent Go jobs with identical step order — `go mod download`, `go vet ./...`, a `gofmt -l .` check, `staticcheck@v0.8.1`, `govulncheck@v1.8.0`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./...` — each caching dependencies against its own `go.sum`.

CI pins Go `1.27.1` for staticcheck compatibility and therefore permits a `govulncheck` failure only when every finding is a Go standard-library CVE fixed in Go 1.27.2 and no module-scoped vulnerability is reported (no `from <n> module` line); any module-level finding still fails the job.

The Go test suites are hermetic — they use injected `getenv` functions and `httptest` rather than live services — and the tests pinning the cross-service conventions are `internal/config/config_test.go` and `internal/logging/logger_test.go` in both modules, `internal/httpapi/middleware_test.go` for `indicator-service`, and `internal/logging/middleware_test.go` plus `internal/server/server_test.go` for `mcp-gateway`.
